paragraphs.title: Daniel's Appointment and Rise in Status

easy.explanation: Darius set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes.
easy.q: How many princes did Darius set over the kingdom?

easy.explanation: The kingdom had three presidents, and Daniel was first among them.
easy.q: How many presidents were over the princes?

easy.explanation: Daniel was preferred because an excellent spirit was in him.
easy.q: Why was Daniel preferred above the other officials?

answers: That the king should have no damage
medium.explanation: The officials were arranged so that the king should have no damage.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the princes giving accounts to the presidents?

answers: Setting him over the whole realm
medium.explanation: The king thought to set Daniel over the whole realm.
medium.q: What did the king think about doing with Daniel?

medium.explanation: Daniel was favored and raised above the other presidents and princes.
medium.q: What does “preferred” mean in this passage?

answers: The king did not know him
challenge.explanation: Considering Daniel for leadership over the whole realm shows the king's confidence in him.
challenge.q: What does Daniel's advancement reveal about the king's view of him?

answers: The kingdom was organized, then Daniel was elevated
The princes were dismissed, then Darius arrived
challenge.explanation: Darius first organized the kingdom, and Daniel then stood out among the officials.
challenge.q: Which order of events is given in these verses?

challenge.explanation: Daniel was distinguished from the others by his excellent spirit.
challenge.q: What contrast is suggested between Daniel and the other officials?

easy.explanation: They could find no occasion, fault, error, or corruption in Daniel.
easy.q: Could the officials find any fault in Daniel's government?

answers: His law and devotion to God
easy.explanation: They decided to find an accusation concerning the law of his God.
easy.q: What part of Daniel's life did the officials target?

easy.explanation: The decree prohibited such petitions for thirty days.
easy.q: For how many days could no one ask a petition of any god or man besides the king?

answers: They found no fault in his work
The king ordered them to do so
medium.explanation: Because Daniel was faithful and blameless, they could find an occasion only concerning his God.
medium.q: Why did the officials focus on Daniel's religion?

answers: Being cast into the lions' den
medium.explanation: Anyone who violated the decree would be cast into the den of lions.
medium.q: What penalty did the decree establish?

medium.explanation: The law of the Medes and Persians was presented as unchangeable.

answers: They had to use Daniel's faith because he had no other fault
They did not know the law
challenge.explanation: Their plan depended on Daniel's unwavering devotion because no ordinary fault could be found.
challenge.q: What weakness in the officials' plan is revealed by their words?

answers: His regular worship would conflict with it
challenge.explanation: Daniel's established practice of praying to God would violate the temporary decree.
challenge.q: Why was the decree especially dangerous for Daniel?

challenge.explanation: The king signed the writing and the decree.
challenge.q: What did Darius do after the writing was presented?

easy.explanation: Daniel prayed and gave thanks before God three times a day.
easy.q: How many times a day did Daniel pray?

easy.explanation: His windows were open toward Jerusalem.
easy.q: Toward what place did Daniel's windows face?

easy.explanation: They found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.
easy.q: What did the officials find Daniel doing?

medium.explanation: Daniel continued his established practice of praying three times a day.
medium.q: What did Daniel do after he knew the decree had been signed?

answers: To show that Daniel had violated it
To ask that it be canceled
medium.explanation: They wanted the king to recognize Daniel's prayer as a violation of the signed decree.
medium.q: Why did the officials remind the king about the decree?

medium.explanation: Supplication is an earnest and humble request made in prayer.
medium.q: What does “supplication” mean in this passage?

answers: His prayer was deliberate and faithful
He wanted to leave the city
challenge.explanation: The open window and regular schedule show Daniel's intentional faithfulness.
challenge.q: What does Daniel's open window toward Jerusalem suggest?

answers: The king's decree conflicts with Daniel's worship
Daniel seeks power from the officials
The officials refuse to obey Darius
challenge.explanation: The decree forbade petitions, while Daniel continued praying to God.
challenge.q: What central conflict appears in these verses?

challenge.explanation: Daniel's consistent and visible practice made him easy to observe.
challenge.q: Why could the officials easily find Daniel praying?

paragraphs.title: Daniel Is Thrown into the Lions' Den

easy.explanation: The king was sore displeased with himself and sought to deliver Daniel.
easy.q: How did Darius react when he heard the accusation?

easy.explanation: The king commanded that Daniel be cast into the den of lions.

answers: He fasted and could not sleep
easy.explanation: Darius passed the night fasting, and his sleep went from him.
easy.q: What did the king do during the night?

answers: The law could not be changed
medium.explanation: The law of the Medes and Persians allowed no decree or statute to be changed.
medium.q: Why could Darius not simply cancel the punishment?

medium.explanation: The king sealed it with his own signet and with the signet of his lords.
medium.q: Who sealed the stone over the den?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Darius lost his sleep because of his distress.
medium.q: What does “his sleep went from him” mean?

answers: He wanted to save Daniel but was bound by the law
He wanted to punish Daniel but feared the lions
He wanted to leave but could not find the door
challenge.explanation: Darius labored to save Daniel, yet the unchangeable decree prevented him.
challenge.q: What inner conflict did Darius experience?

answers: So the situation could not be changed
So the lions could be fed
challenge.explanation: The seals ensured that the purpose concerning Daniel would not be changed.
challenge.q: Why were the seals placed on the stone?

answers: He was deeply concerned for him
He was pleased with his punishment
challenge.explanation: Fasting, sleeplessness, and his early visit show the king's concern for Daniel.
challenge.q: What does Darius's night reveal about his feelings toward Daniel?

paragraphs.title: Deliverance and Punishment of the Accusers

easy.explanation: Daniel respectfully answered, “O king, live for ever.”
easy.q: What did Daniel say to the king in the morning?

easy.explanation: Daniel said that God had sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths.

answers: They were cast into the den
easy.explanation: The king cast the accusers, their children, and their wives into the den.
easy.q: What happened to the men who accused Daniel?

answers: God sent an angel to shut their mouths
medium.explanation: Daniel said that God's angel shut the lions' mouths so they did not hurt him.
medium.q: Why did the lions not hurt Daniel?

medium.explanation: Daniel declared that he had done no hurt before the king.
medium.q: What did Daniel say about his conduct toward the king?

medium.explanation: The king rejoiced because Daniel was taken from the den without any hurt.
medium.q: Why was the king exceeding glad?

answers: Daniel was unharmed, while they were destroyed
Daniel was punished, while they were honored
challenge.explanation: Daniel emerged safely, but the accusers were overcome by the lions.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between Daniel and his accusers?

answers: No manner of hurt was found upon him
challenge.explanation: Daniel came out without any injury despite being in the lions' den.
challenge.q: What proves that Daniel's deliverance was extraordinary?

answers: He was innocent before God and loyal to the king
He had rejected both God and the king
He had served only the officials
challenge.explanation: Daniel said that innocence was found in him before God and that he had done no hurt to the king.
challenge.q: How do Daniel's statements describe his faithfulness?

easy.explanation: Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages throughout the earth.
easy.q: To whom did Darius send his proclamation?

easy.explanation: Darius proclaimed that Daniel's God is the living God.
Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
easy.q: Under which rulers did Daniel prosper?

medium.explanation: Darius decreed that people should tremble and fear before the God of Daniel.
medium.q: What did Darius command the people to do before Daniel's God?

medium.explanation: The proclamation calls God living, steadfast forever, and able to deliver and rescue.
medium.q: Which qualities of God does Darius emphasize?

medium.explanation: Darius says that God's kingdom shall not be destroyed.
medium.q: What does “shall not be destroyed” describe?

answers: It declared His power to all peoples
It limited worship to Daniel's household
It made Him one of the king's officials
challenge.explanation: The proclamation presented God's living and everlasting power before all the nations.
challenge.q: How did the proclamation affect the public recognition of Daniel's God?

answers: The rescue from the lions demonstrated God's delivering power
It denied that a miracle occurred
challenge.explanation: Darius based the proclamation on God's rescue of Daniel from the lions.
challenge.q: How is the proclamation connected to Daniel's deliverance?

answers: His success continued under different rulers
challenge.explanation: Daniel prospered under both Darius and Cyrus the Persian.
challenge.q: What does Daniel's continued prosperity show?
